text:
alex: Heads-up — after upgrading a few boxes to NVIDIA driver 540 the nightly perf regression surfaced for convo workloads with long prefixes.

maria: saw that on staging too. timeline: driver 539 -> 540 rolled last night. which metric regressed?

alex: p50 latency on streaming gen spikes ~20% for seqlen 256 workloads, throughput drops under medium batching (batch=4).

cheng: interestingly, our kernel picker flipped to the FP8 fastpath at seqlen 64 boundaries. trace from the runtime: 
```
[info] device_cap = {sm=92, hw_fp8=true, hw_bf16=true}
[debug] choose_kernel(model=redwood-xl, seqlen=256) -> kernel=matmul_fp8_tiled_v2
[warn] kvcache_mode = prefetched_contiguous -> thrash_ratio=0.42
```

ravi: that hw_fp8 flag shouldn't be true on those cards (they're A100-LX configured w/o fp8 firmware). driver 540 seems to expose a capability bit we didn't account for.

selina: do we have a repro pod + profile? can run nvprof / nsight quick.

alex: repro on aml-staging-3 running the nightly model. attached perf snippet (top lines):
```
GPU stall reason: memory_throttle 58% -> increased L2 misses
SM eff: 0.62 -> down from 0.89 on 539
KV cache read latency: mean=1.4ms -> 2.8ms
```

perf-bot: perf/regression:detected model=redwood-xl seqlen=256 p50+20% (compare: 1777680000 -> 1777770000)

maria: hypothesis: kernel picker sees hw_fp8 and picks fp8 matmul that uses a different tiling + shared memory pattern. that pattern reduces asynchronous KV cache prefetch locality for long prefixes, causing extra device-host syncs.

cheng: yep. the fp8 kernel prefers contiguous KV layout and assumes 32B stride; our current KV cache layout for long-prefix streaming uses chunked pages with 64B stride. mismatch increases bank conflicts.

ravi: quick mitigation: force fallback to bf16 path for cards that report fp8 but are pre-540 firmware. we can gate by driver version or by running a small microbench at startup: run tiny_fp8_probe() -> verify correctness and perf.

selina: any quick config change? I can push a canary.

alex: suggestion: add a runtime autotune step on first startup per-GPU: run two microbenchmarks (seqlen=64 and seqlen=256) and record kernel latency, choose path. store results in /var/lib/redwood/gpu-probe-cache.json. snippet: 
```
probe: {
  seqlens: [64,256],
  trials: 3,
  record: [{kernel, ms, sm_eff}]
}
```

maria: sounds good. also add a safety: if kvcache thrash_ratio > 0.2 switch to alternate kernel immediately.

cheng: long-term we should make kernel picker aware of kvcache layout and batching heuristics (not only sm+flags+seqlen). reorder preference: correctness -> kvcache_compat -> latency.

ravi: I'll open a small PR to: (1) add microprobe, (2) add driver-version override env REDWOOD_FORCE_FP8=false, (3) add runtime thrash detector.

selina: can we also add a perf regression alert rule that tags driver package changes? so infra gets pinged.

alex: yes — tag it as infra:driver and cc infra-team. For this thread: Can someone run the microprobe on aml-staging-3 and confirm fallback fixes it?

maria: running now, will post numbers in ~10m.

perf-bot: job/probe-aml-staging-3 started (id: probe-2026-03-18-01)

alex: thanks. keeping this here so we don't lose the correlation between driver 540 and kernel flip. :thumbsup:

maria: quick update: microprobe shows fp8 kernel is ~15% faster at seqlen=64 but ~25% slower at seqlen=256 (due to KV thrash). forcing BF16 brings seqlen256 latency back to baseline. posting logs to #eng-runtime-artifacts shortly.

cheng: perfect. next steps: PR + canary + add thrash detector + infra alert. I'll help review the PR.

ravi: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/432 (draft) — implements probe + env override + thrash detector.

alex: excellent. after canary and a few days of telemetry we can roll to prod if stable.

selina: tagging @infra for driver rollout rollback option.

perf-bot: action required: perf team follow-up in 48h.
